comments.text: This is not the people problem it is the Government needs to help them

replies.author: @TheGlobalTruth04
replies.text: You make an important point. Many of these challenges are shaped by policies and the support systems people have access to, so government action can play a major role in improving the situation. Thanks for sharing your perspective. 🙏

comments.author: @Globallife.documentary
comments.text: This isn't just a Lagos problem—from Manila to Rio, urban inequality looks the exact same.

replies.author: @TheGlobalTruth04
replies.text: Absolutely. Different cities, same pattern—rapid growth, unequal access to housing and services, and whole communities being left behind. Lagos is just one example of a much bigger global urban challenge.

comments.author: @AtlasDiscover1
comments.text: The vast expanse of the Lagos Lagoon surrounding Makoko creates such an extraordinary and surreal waterscape! Seeing an entire sprawling community harmonizing directly with the open water and changing tides is truly unbelievable.

replies.author: @TheGlobalTruth04
replies.text: Beautifully said. Makoko’s relationship with the lagoon is truly remarkable—the water isn’t just a backdrop, but part of the community’s daily life, movement, and identity. It’s a place that really challenges the way we think about cities and how people adapt to their environment.
